A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same U-NOTB research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic barycenter experiments, outlier and class-imbalance tests, and MNIST shape-color results, including numerical errors and acceptance rates.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Gaussian benchmark experiments, runtime measurements and FFHQ image-manipulation results. Some Gaussian baseline scores are explicitly reused from prior work.

M1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a substantive adaptation that learns multiple barycenters simultaneously by conditioning transport maps, potentials and the congruence parameter on barycenter weights. It introduces residual latent-space maps using StyleGAN2, e4e and transformers. The core solver remains, with corrections to Algorithm 1's printed map-loss sign and the congruence offset in Section 4.2.

E1.justification: v2 adds balanced and semi-unbalanced Gaussian barycenter benchmarks and FFHQ age transformation under gender imbalance (Appendix D). These substantially extend v1's two-dimensional toy/mixture and MNIST shape-color coverage to computable-reference Gaussian problems and real face images.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds comparisons with EgBary, WIN and FCWB alongside NOTB; the continuous baseline scores are attributed to an earlier publication. Table 7 introduces a global latent-direction baseline. Original UOTM, Mini-Batch UOT and NOTB comparisons remain; corrected NOTB citations do not establish a baseline replacement.

E3.justification: New Gaussian protocols use computable reference barycenters, dimension and unbalancedness sweeps, barycentric projections, and L2-UVP/Bures-Wasserstein UVP metrics. FFHQ introduces a random 90/10 split and evaluation at interpolation weight t=0.9, using accepted images for U-NOTB but the full test set for baselines. Timing measurements specify 1000 synthetic or 220 shape-color samples. The original hyperparameter table is retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds sensitivity analyses testing Gaussian accuracy against unbalancedness and dimension, including approximation of the balanced limit. FFHQ analyses examine accepted versus rejected samples and their gender composition (Figures 6–7). Tables 2–3 additionally investigate computational overhead. The original outlier and class-imbalance analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seed specifications, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both mention seed sensitivity as a limitation without quantifying it; the added performance tables do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the MNIST acceptance rates remain unchanged, but v2 corrects the toy-results summary from winning every comparison to three of four. New results include Gaussian errors and runtimes. Table 7 reports 88.0% FFHQ accuracy on 592 accepted images, with 67.9% acceptance; baseline accuracies of 69.8% and 63.4% use all 872 images. These are new experiments, not improvements to v1 scores under identical settings.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 3 and its Appendix A.3 proof relating conditional-plan Wasserstein error to two optimization gaps under strong-convexity and positive-derivative assumptions. It also adds a superlinear divergence-generator assumption, explicitly handles absolute continuity, and revises boundedness and support arguments in existing proofs. v1's cited auxiliary Theorem 3 is retained as Theorem 4.

C1.justification: The central claims of a continuous robust SUOT barycenter solver, general-cost applicability and robustness remain. The introduction now explicitly includes quality bounds for recovered transport plans among the contributions, extending the earlier general claim of a theoretical foundation.

C2.justification: v2 explains when approximate optimization should recover accurate plans while acknowledging that strong convexity is not guaranteed in practice. It adds interpretations of Gaussian error saturation, rejection-induced inference overhead and selective FFHQ rejection as imbalance correction. Most original limitations move to Appendix E, but the explicit statement that convergence properties are unestablished is removed.

D1.justification: v2 first provides a public code address, identifies PyTorch and points to README reproduction instructions. It adds hardware and runtime disclosures and detailed FFHQ implementation information, including transformer architecture, conditioning, learning rates, batch size and training iterations. Original experimental details are retained in Appendix C.

R1.justification: Targeted additions cover Hellinger–Kantorovich barycenters, sliced unbalanced OT, further neural solvers, the Gaussian reference algorithm and FFHQ components. The principal positioning as the first continuous robust barycenter approach remains. Moving the existing neural-OT survey to Appendix B is primarily organizational.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 makes local language, notation and cross-reference corrections, updates affiliations and publication headers, and moves the neural-OT survey and limitations into appendices. The substantial new scientific sections do not amount to a wholesale rewrite of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds a prominent explanatory schematic, accepted/rejected FFHQ image panels, and tables for timings, Gaussian comparisons, FFHQ accuracy and FFHQ settings. Existing experimental figures remain with caption/index corrections. The original hyperparameter table moves into the implementation appendix instead of interrupting a proof.

improvement.justification: Computable-reference Gaussian validation, broader comparisons, conditional plan-error analysis and concrete code/runtime/implementation disclosures address substantial validation and reproducibility gaps in v1. Correcting the toy-result overclaim also improves accuracy. These gains outweigh limitations in the new FFHQ evidence, which compares different evaluation subsets and states inconsistent gender proportions. The theoretical bound remains conditional and does not establish training convergence.
